title: Irumudi Crosses ₹215 Crore Worldwide as Ravi Teja Scores Biggest Blockbuster of His Career
excerpt: The Telugu action drama has grossed ₹187 crore in India alone after 17 days, with the ₹200 crore domestic milestone now within reach — all without hiked ticket prices.
body:
• Irumudi has grossed over ₹215 crore worldwide and ₹187 crore in India after 17 days, making it Ravi Teja's highest-grossing film ever.
  • The Shiva Nirvana-directed Telugu action drama, produced by Mythri Movie Makers on a ₹40 crore budget, opened to ₹24.20 crore worldwide on day one — a career-best for Ravi Teja.
  • The film collected ₹107 crore in its first week and ₹68 crore in week two, holding strong despite competition from Yash's Toxic, which released five days later.
  • If Irumudi crosses ₹200 crore in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, it will join an exclusive club of just seven films — and be the first to reach that mark without hiked ticket rates.

Ravi Teja's Irumudi has emerged as one of the biggest Telugu box office hits of 2026, crossing the ₹215 crore mark worldwide and closing in on the ₹200 crore milestone at the Indian box office. The film, which released on August 21, collected ₹5.75 crore on its third Saturday, taking its Indian gross to ₹187.25 crore — a figure that would have seemed improbable for the actor just weeks ago.

A Career-Defining Opening

Irumudi opened to ₹24.20 crore worldwide on day one, with ₹17.20 crore coming from India alone. It was the biggest opening of Ravi Teja's three-decade career. The first week delivered ₹107 crore in India, and the second week added another ₹68 crore, reflecting the kind of sustained hold that blockbusters rarely manage.

The film's domestic gross now sits at ₹187.25 crore, with around ₹169 crore coming from the Telugu states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Based on current trends, trade analysts expect the film to cross ₹193-194 crore by the end of its third weekend and enter the ₹200 crore club on weekdays.

"Till now, only seven films have managed to gross ₹200 crore or more in AP/TS, and almost all of them, except Baahubali 2, did so with hiked ticket rates."

— Pinkvilla box office analysis

Holding Ground Against Toxic

When the release date was announced, industry observers predicted a difficult clash with Yash's Toxic, which arrived on August 26 — just five days later. The conventional wisdom was that Irumudi would be forced to reschedule. Instead, Ravi Teja's film held its ground, maintaining strong occupancy even as Toxic competed for screens. Many centres that removed Irumudi on Wednesday to accommodate the new release brought it back by Monday, and it resumed collecting strongly.

The territorial breakdown tells the story of a film that dominated its home market. AP/TS accounts for ₹169 crore of the total India gross, with Nizam alone contributing ₹81 crore. Karnataka has been a pleasant surprise at ₹13.50 crore, though Tamil Nadu and Kerala remain relatively soft.

What Made Irumudi Work

Written and directed by Shiva Nirvana, Irumudi tells the story of Trinadh Rama Kasu, an alcoholic plantain farmer who undertakes the sacred Ayyappa Deeksha pilgrimage for his young daughter, Manikanta. The father-daughter bond anchors a narrative that moves into darker territory as the story unfolds, dealing with child exploitation and institutional complicity in a rural setting.

Critics have been largely positive. Cinema Express rated the film 3.5 out of 5, calling it "a gripping family drama that blends a socially relevant subject, Ayyappa Deeksha, and family emotions effectively." Filmfare gave it 3 out of 5, praising Ravi Teja's "restrained performance" while noting that "predictable villains and uneven emotional beats prevent it from becoming as powerful as it could have been."

Baby Nakshathra's performance as Manikanta has been singled out as a highlight, as has G.V. Prakash Kumar's score, particularly the devotional tracks associated with Lord Ayyappa. Vishnu Sarma's cinematography, shot largely on location in Sileru on the Odisha-Andhra Pradesh border, has drawn praise for its authentic feel.

What the Numbers Mean for Ravi Teja

Before Irumudi, Ravi Teja had been coming off a string of underwhelming box office results. None of his previous films had posted first-day collections anywhere near ₹17 crore. The actor, who has been a reliable mass entertainer in Telugu cinema since the early 2000s, had seen his market position erode as younger stars expanded their audience base.

Irumudi's performance represents a genuine comeback. With a production budget of ₹40 crore, the film has already returned more than five times its cost at the box office. The overseas collection of approximately ₹20.50 crore — another career best — confirms that Ravi Teja's fanbase extends well beyond the Telugu states.

What's Next

The film benefits from a clear runway over the next two weeks, with no significant Telugu release competing for screens during the Janmashtami and Ganesh Chaturthi holiday period. Trade analysts expect Irumudi to finish its theatrical run somewhere between ₹230 and ₹250 crore worldwide. The ₹200 crore domestic milestone, which seemed distant at the start of the third week, now looks like a matter of when, not if.
